title: Introduction to Administrative Law — Origin, Nature, Scope and Functions

content.overview: Administrative law is the body of law that regulates the powers, procedures and accountability of public authorities. It grew with the expansion of the administrative state and is concerned with keeping public power within legal bounds while enabling effective governance.
content.glance: Define administrative law; state its origin and necessity; outline nature and scope; list principal functions (control of power, protection of rights, facilitation of administration); link to constitutional judicial review.
content.study: Administrative law emerged as the modern state assumed welfare, regulatory and licensing functions that the ordinary courts and classical separation-of-powers model could not fully accommodate. Its core concerns are the source and limits of administrative power, the procedures by which that power is exercised, and the remedies available when power is exceeded or abused. In India the subject is constitutionally anchored in Articles 14, 19, 21, 32 and 226 and in the body of statutes creating specialised authorities and tribunals. Current-law framing: ground the analysis in the Constitution and the relevant parent statute. Do not treat BSA 2023 as the source of this doctrine.

sections.heading: Origin and Necessity
sections.body: The growth of the welfare and regulatory state required specialised rules governing administrative power, discretion and accountability.

sections.heading: Nature of Administrative Law
sections.body: It is public law concerned with the organisation, powers, duties and control of administrative authorities.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Includes delegated legislation, administrative adjudication, discretion, natural justice, judicial review, tribunals, liability and non-judicial controls.

sections.heading: Functions
sections.body: Control of public power; protection of individual rights; facilitation of efficient administration within legal limits.

sections.heading: Constitutional Anchoring
sections.body: Indian administrative law is shaped by fundamental rights, judicial review under Articles 32 and 226, and the rule-of-law principle.

examples.title: Licensing power
examples.body: A statute empowers an authority to grant or refuse licences. Administrative law supplies the standards of fairness, relevance of considerations and judicial review that constrain that power.

examples.title: Rule-making
examples.body: A ministry frames subordinate rules under a parent Act. Administrative law tests whether the rules stay within the parent power and respect constitutional limits.

hypotheticals.question: Is administrative law only about controlling the executive?
hypotheticals.analysis: Control is central, but the subject also facilitates lawful administration and structures remedies and procedures.

hypotheticals.question: Does administrative law replace constitutional law?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. It operates within and is shaped by the Constitution, especially fundamental rights and judicial review.

distinctions.title: Administrative law vs constitutional law
distinctions.left: Detailed rules governing administrative power, procedure and remedies
distinctions.right: Fundamental structure, rights and allocation of state power

misconceptions.correction: It draws on statutes, the Constitution, delegated legislation and judicial decisions.

misconceptions.trap: Administrative law exists only to obstruct government.
misconceptions.correction: It both controls power and enables lawful, effective administration.

cases.name: A.K. Kraipak v Union of India
cases.issue: Application of natural justice to administrative action.
cases.ratioDecidendi: The dividing line between administrative and quasi-judicial functions is thin; fairness applies where rights are affected.
cases.holding: Natural justice applied on the facts.
cases.relevance: Foundational Indian authority on the reach of administrative-law fairness.

cases.name: Tata Cellular v Union of India
cases.issue: Scope of judicial review of administrative action.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Courts review legality and rationality of the decision-making process, not ordinary commercial judgment.
cases.holding: Review standards applied to the administrative decision.
cases.relevance: Leading authority on the scope of judicial review.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should an introduction-to-administrative-law problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Define the subject. II. State origin and necessity. III. Outline scope and functions. IV. Link to constitutional judicial review. V. Apply to the facts.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Definition; constitutional anchoring; applicable doctrine (discretion, fairness, review); precise relief.

examTips: Link every doctrine to constitutional anchors.
content.migrationNote: Substantive enhancement. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

enhancement.definition: Administrative law regulates the powers, procedures and accountability of public authorities within the constitutional framework.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Public power must be authorised by law, exercised fairly and reviewed for legality.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Constitution of India; parent administrative statutes.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Administrative law grew with the administrative state and remains constitutionally anchored in India.
enhancement.problemApplication: Define; state necessity; apply relevant doctrine to the facts.
keyTakeaways: Administrative law controls and facilitates public power.
Scope covers discretion, fairness, review and liability.

verification.note: Doctrine-level content; case-law verification separate; no new citations invented.
